Encompasses: Loss of tribal knowledge, lack of human provenance for code, and degradation of mental models. 
Excludes: General developer turnover or poor documentation practices.

This erosion occurs because AI-generated code enters the system without any developer having made the algorithmic choices or considered the trade-offs.

unmapped_concepts.reason: This concept captures the unique sociotechnical state of 'never-acquired' knowledge, which is distinct from 'deferred' knowledge.

unmapped_concepts.Safetyist Interpretation: Safetyists would interpret this as a critical systemic risk, arguing that the lack of human understanding makes the system inherently un-auditable and prone to catastrophic failure during maintenance.
unmapped_concepts.Skeptic Interpretation: Skeptics would interpret this as evidence of the 'hollowing out' of engineering teams, where reliance on AI leads to a loss of the fundamental skills required to manage complex systems.

unmapped_concepts.concept: A maintenance crisis occurs when the effort required to safely modify code begins to exceed the value delivered by new features. The document hypothesizes that AI-generated code may reach this threshold faster due to compounding comprehension difficulties.

unmapped_concepts.Safetyist Interpretation: Safetyists would interpret this as a critical risk indicator, arguing that organizations must slow down AI adoption to avoid reaching this threshold and incurring catastrophic maintenance failures.
